grammar.title: 过去将来时 (Future in the Past)
grammar.structure: would + 动词原形 / was/were going to + 动词原形
grammar.definition: 表示从过去某时看来将要发生的动作或存在的状态，常用于宾语从句中 当主句谓语是过去时态时（如said, thought, knew等），宾语从句中要使用过去将来时表示当时认为将要发生的事

examples.en: Right from the start there was trouble with the Hubble. (客观事实)
examples.zh: 从一开始哈勃望远镜就有问题。

examples.en: NASA was going to put the telescope right. (当时计划要做的)
examples.zh: 美国国家航空航天局准备把望远镜修好。

examples.en: By the time you read this, the Hubble's eagle eye will have sent us thousands of wonderful pictures. (将来完成时)
examples.zh: 到你读到这个的时候，哈勃的鹰眼将已经给我们发送了成千上万张精彩的照片。

grammar.title: 将来进行时 (Future Continuous)
grammar.definition: 表示在将来某一时刻或某段时间正在进行的动作 用于描述在将来某个时间正在发生的动作，强调动作的进行性

examples.en: It will soon be sending us the clearest pictures of the stars.
examples.zh: 它很快将给我们发送最清晰的星星照片。

examples.en: The shuttle Endeavour will be taking the astronauts to the Hubble.
examples.zh: 奋进号航天飞机将把宇航员送往哈勃望远镜。

grammar.title: 将来完成时 (Future Perfect)
grammar.definition: 表示在将来某一时刻之前已经完成的动作 用于描述到将来某个时间为止已经完成的事情，常与by the time等时间状语连用

examples.en: By the time you read this, the Hubble's eagle eye will have sent us thousands of wonderful pictures.
examples.zh: 到你读到这个的时候，哈勃的鹰眼将已经给我们发送了成千上万张精彩的照片。

translation: 哈勃望远镜于1990年4月20日由国家航空航天局发射升空，耗资10多亿美元。从最开始哈勃望远镜就有问题。它传送给我们的图像很令人失望，因为它的主要镜子有误差。国家航天局准备纠正这一错误，为此将把4名宇航员送入太空修复望远镜。“奋进”号航天飞机将把宇航员送上哈勃。当宇航员进行必要的修复工作时，“奋进”号上的一只机器手将抓住望远镜并托住它。当然，哈勃位于地球的大气层之外，因此，它很快就会给我们传送我们所见到过的、有关行星和远距离星系的最清晰的照片。哈勃将告诉我们有关宇宙的年龄和大小的许多事情。等到你读到这篇文章时，敏锐的哈勃望远镜已经为我们送来了成千上万张精彩的照片。

text.title: Trouble with the Hubble哈勃望远镜的困境

lines.en: The Hubble telescope was launched into space by NASA on April 20,1990 at a cost of over a billion dollars.
Right from the start there was trouble with the Hubble.
The pictures it sent us were very disappointing because its main mirror was faulty!
NASA is now going to put the telescope right, so it will soon be sending up four astronauts to repair it.
The shuttle Endeavour will be taking the astronauts to the Hubble.
A robot-arm from the Endeavour will grab the telescope and hold it while the astronauts make the necessary repairs.
Of course, the Hubble is above the earth's atmosphere, so it will soon be sending us the clearest pictures of the stars and distant galaxies that we have ever seen.
The Hubble will tell us a great deal about the age and size of the universe.
By the time you read this, the Hubble's eagle eye will have sent us thousands and thousands of wonderful pictures.
